newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt sends bank selloff plan back to finmin.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt sends bank selloff plan back to finmin.

text.p: The Czech government on Wednesday sent a plan to privatise state stakes in major domestic banks back to the Finance Ministry for further work, Finance Minister Ivan Pilip told a news conference.
He said that the ministry would make revisions and deliver the plan for government approval with the aim of submitting the final proposal to parliament in September.
"The government supported the intention of speeding up steps for the privatisation of banks and directed the finance ministry to complete such material," Pilip said.

He declined to say what the contentious points of the ministry's original plan, which was drawn up and signed by Pilip earlier this month and called for remaining state shares in three of the four largest domestic banks to be sold.

The ministry said that it would first seek a "strategic," which analysts widely believe to mean a "foreign," partner to take stakes in the largest commercial bank, Komercni Banka a.s. and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s..
